<task> Read-only adversarial code review of git commits 0b2f21f..84a26f1 in /home/motoko/workspace/magomap (main). Do NOT edit files, commit, or change the git index or HEAD. Use only read-only git commands (git log/diff/show). Context: Codex previously reviewed f25c52c..0b2f21f (magomap backend: pnpm monorepo, Kysely over Cloudflare D1 / Postgres via Hyperdrive / better-sqlite3, Hono Worker). It found 7 issues: 1. Retrying a clock-clamped mutation overwrote newer diary content. 2. Writes rejected concurrently in SQL were reported as applied. 3. A concurrent place delete hid an accepted note. 4. Tombstones raced concurrent inserts. 5. A superseded import run could still commit. 6. Finishing a list exceeded Cloudflare limits (80 statements, a JSON parameter near 3 MB). 7. A refused place update still appended location history. The fix (commit d1bd3e4) introduces an optimistic per-user write: withUserWrite in packages/db/src/stores/sync.ts. - It reads users.change_seq, runs a decide step (pre-reads and builds statements), then executes one atomic batch: [claim, ...statements, check]. - claim is UPDATE users SET change_seq = current+1, write_token = <fresh UUIDv7> WHERE id = ? AND change_seq = current [AND claimGuard]. - Every statement carries a guard: EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM users WHERE id = ? AND write_token = <token>). - check selects write_token. If it isnt our token, nothing was written and decide re-runs, up to 5 times, then WriteConflictError becomes a 503.
- Rows get seq = current+1 directly.
- Import functions (packages/db/src/stores/importRuns.ts) use a claimGuard requiring the run still to be running.
- Far-future clientUpdatedAt (more than now + 60 s) is now rejected as invalid instead of clamped.
- Migration 0003 adds users.write_token.
- Regression tests: packages/db/src/stores/concurrency.test.ts, which interleaves another write between the pre-read and the batch. Also apps/api/src/errors.ts.

Try to break it:
- Can two writers both pass the claim, on D1 (batches serialized, executed as a transaction) and on Postgres (READ COMMITTED transaction, row lock from the UPDATE)?
- Is any write statement unguarded? Check bulkUpsertQuerys guard placement in INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE guard ON CONFLICT ... for both SQLite and Postgres. - Are any decisions still based on data read before change_seq was read? - Are there writers that dont go through withUserWrite but change synced tables, so their changes dont bump change_seq? Examples: startImportRun, deleteAccount, session code. - Can the import or the 503 path lose or duplicate a write? - Is the result reported to the client correct on every path, including the retry loop? - Is the first-batch check of results.at(-1).rows reliable on D1, Postgres and better-sqlite3? - Are the new statement and parameter counts within D1 limits (at most 100 bound params per statement, about 50 statements per request)? - Does the clock rejection interact badly with the client (see docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-19-02-magomap-pwa.md Task 2 sync rules)? Also check that the 7 original findings are actually fixed. Tests may be run read-only: pnpm -r test. Postgres tests need TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://magomap:magomap@localhost:5432/magomap_test; the container should be running, though your sandbox may block localhost. </task> <grounding_rules> Anchor every claim in code you read or tests you ran. Label hypotheses as such. </grounding_rules> <structured_output_contract> Report findings ranked Critical / Important / Minor, each with file:line, a concrete failing scenario, and a fix. End with a verdict. </structured_output_contract>
